compatibility.title: Which Models Use the P510?

failures.title: Land Rover P510 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Mild-Hybrid (MHEV) Electrical System Faults
items.whatHappens: The 48-volt belt-integrated starter generator (BISG) or associated DC-DC converter can develop faults, leading to "Reduced Engine Power" warnings, inability to crank, or complete no-start conditions. This is the most frequently reported issue for this modern architecture.
items.repairVsReplace: Module, software, or BISG replacement is a standard diagnostic repair and does not require a full Land Rover P510 engine replacement unless catastrophic electrical damage has occurred.

items.title: Cooling System Leaks (Water Pump / Thermostat Housing)
items.whatHappens: The integrated water pump and thermostat housing can develop internal or external leaks due to plastic degradation under repeated heat cycles. Symptoms include unexplained coolant loss, overheating warnings, and visible coolant pooling.
items.repairVsReplace: Water pump and housing replacement is a standard maintenance fix. However, if the leak is ignored and leads to severe overheating, the cylinder head may warp, necessitating a full Land Rover P510 engine replacement. Read our full coolant system failure guide.

items.title: Turbocharger and Supercharger Wear
items.whatHappens: The twin-charged setup is complex. The turbocharger wastegate can develop a rattle, or supercharger coupler wear can cause a distinct knocking noise under load, leading to boost leaks and reduced power.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbocharger or supercharger component replacement is a standard repair and does not require a full engine replacement unless debris has entered the oil system and caused bearing damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: As a very recent architecture (2020+), long-term mechanical failure patterns are still emerging. However, early MHEV electrical gremlins and cooling system leaks are the most documented issues, and later production runs have seen minor software and seal revisions to mitigate these .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the P510
variants.intro: The P510 is Land Rover's specific high-output designation for the twin-charged 3.0-litre Ingenium inline-6 petrol engine. Confirming your exact code is critical because, while it shares its core architecture with lower-output variants, internal components, forced-induction plumbing, and engine management are not universally interchangeable. WHERE TO FIND THE CODE: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover. It will also be explicitly listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Code" or "Engine Capacity", and can be decoded directly from your 17-character VIN. COMMONLY CONFUSED CODES: - P400 / AJ20P6: The lower-output (395-400 hp) single-turbo variant of the 3.0L Ingenium inline-6. Externally similar in layout, but it lacks the supercharger assembly and has different ECU mapping, making it a non-straight swap. - 508PS: The older 5.0-litre supercharged V8. This is a completely different architecture (V8 vs Inline-6) with entirely different mounting points, wiring harnesses, and physical dimensions, making it physically incompatible. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: Attempting to swap a single-turbo P400 or a V8 508PS long block into a P510 chassis without extensive, custom fabrication, ECU remapping, and wiring loom replacement will result in persistent fault codes, severe drivability issues, and potential sensor incompatibility. CLOSING LINE: Not 100% sure? Enter your registration above - we'll confirm your exact P510 fitment before any quotes are sent.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement P510 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Land Rover P510 engine is only advisable if it comes with comprehensive, documented proof that the MHEV electrical system and cooling system have been proactively maintained or updated. Given the high performance and electrical complexity of this engine, the risk of inheriting hidden electrical faults is significant without this history. Explore our vetted used Land Rover P510 engine network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Land Rover P510 engine is the most balanced and recommended choice for the majority of owners. A quality, specialist-led rebuild will systematically address the known weak points: verified turbocharger and supercharger health, refreshed cooling system components, and tested MHEV integration, alongside all critical gaskets and seals. This effectively resets the engine's reliability clock and is the most cost-effective way to secure long-term peace of mind. Compare reconditioned Land Rover P510 engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples, vehicles that have suffered from overheating, or if the cylinder bores show measurable scoring. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, a reground crankshaft, and a complete refresh of the oil pump and forced-induction assemblies, ensuring the engine can reliably handle another 100,000+ miles of heavy-duty use. View rebuilt Land Rover P510 engine specifications.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Buying through the EnginesMarket network means you can opt for a full supply and fit service, with the replacement engine installed by a Land Rover specialist and backed by a nationwide warranty. Learn more about supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The Land Rover P510 is typically found in host vehicles (like the Defender OCTA and F-Pace SVR) valued between £80,000 and £120,000+, heavily dependent on condition, mileage, and specification. For these modern, ultra-high-value chassis, a £5,500+ reconditioned Land Rover P510 engine replacement represents a highly viable investment (well under 15% of the vehicle's total current market value), making replacement financially sound and strongly recommended over evaluating scrap value.

items.question: How much does a Land Rover P510 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Land Rover P510 engine typically costs between £5,500 and £8,500 for supply only. Fitted costs through an independent specialist will add approximately £780-£1,040 in labour. Used units are available from £3,000 but carry a higher risk of inherited MHEV or forced-induction wear.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the P510?
items.answer: The most documented issues are 48V mild-hybrid (MHEV) electrical system faults and cooling system leaks. MHEV faults can trigger 'Reduced Engine Power' warnings or no-start conditions. Water pump and thermostat housing leaks are also common between 60,000 and 100,000 miles.
bullets: MHEV faults can trigger "Reduced Engine Power" warnings or no-start conditions.

items.question: Which models use the P510 engine?
items.answer: The P510 is fitted to the Land Rover Defender OCTA (L663) and the Jaguar F-Pace SVR (X761) from 2020 onwards. It serves as the flagship high-output twin-charged petrol option for these specific performance variants. It shares its core architecture with lower-output 3.0L Ingenium inline-6 variants.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned P510 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Land Rover P510 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the complexity and high replacement cost of the twin-charged and MHEV systems. A proper rebuild will systematically verify turbocharger and supercharger health, refresh cooling components, and test MHEV integration. A used unit is only advisable with comprehensive, documented proof of proactive maintenance.
